overall: Wednesday (July 15) is expected to be a partly sunny day with afternoon convective storm chances (40% PoP after 11am), representing a notable improvement from today's stormier pattern. The NWS pegs the high near 86°F, but storm activity and cloud cover through the afternoon could suppress daytime heating. Conditions are broadly unsettled but not severe.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is exceptionally wide and is the dominant risk factor: ECMWF sits at ~80°F while GFS (~88°F) and HRRR (~89°F) are nearly 9°F warmer, with NBM and WEATHER_COM clustering near 84-85°F as a middle ground. This large inter-model divergence — likely driven by disagreement on storm timing and cloud cover suppression — is the primary source of forecast uncertainty and makes confident temperature prediction very difficult.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model's expected TMAX of 82.4°F and dominant even-bucket probability at 80-81°F (20.8%) suggest the lower end of the range is most likely, anchored by afternoon storm potential limiting solar heating. The active Kalshi market uses ODD buckets with the top bucket at 89-90°F (13.0%), which is in strong tension with the ensemble consensus and is flagged as Tier 4 (Poor signals - AVOID) with only 32% expected accuracy — the high end implied by GFS/HRRR would require storms to stay suppressed, which is uncertain. Best estimate for TMAX is around 84°F, splitting the NWS guidance (~86°F) and the ensemble model (82.4°F), with low confidence given the extreme model spread.
